sites.name: Gramercy Park Dunleith Mound Group
sites.description: The park, situated on a high bluff overlooking the Mississippi River valley, includes 20 mounds still standing of an original group of 26 Middle Woodland conical mounds.

sites.name: Galena & U.S. Grant Museum
sites.description: Exhibits include Native American artifacts recovered from the Galena area along with regional history collections.

sites.name: Apple River Fort State Historic Site
sites.description: An interpretive center relates the story of the Black Hawk War, as well as the interactions between the Sauk and Mesquakie (Fox) and lead miners in the early 19th century.

sites.name: Wapello Land & Water Reserve
sites.description: This reserve preserves Woodland and Mississippian archaeological sites within a protected landscape along the upper Mississippi region.

sites.name: Macktown Living History Education Center
sites.hours: Second Sunday each month; other visits by reservation
sites.description: The education center highlights archaeology investigating the 1838 to 1850 settlement, as well as Native habitations dating back 10,000 years; volunteers are welcome at annual summer field work.

sites.name: Carl and Myrna Nygren Wetland Preserve
sites.description: This wetland preserve includes Native American mound sites within a restored natural landscape.

sites.name: Beattie Mound Group
sites.description: This Late Woodland effigy mound group is preserved within a public park setting in Rockford.

sites.name: Thomson Mound
sites.description: This Woodland period mound stands along the Mississippi River corridor near Thomson.

sites.name: Jarrett Prairie Center
sites.hours: Mon-Fri 8AM-4:30PM; Tue & Thu until 8PM; Sat 9AM-4PM; Sun 1-4PM
sites.description: Museum displays include information on the archaeology of the Rock River area of Ogle County, including interpretation along the Diana Nora Nature Trail.

sites.name: Albany Mounds State Historic Site
sites.description: This large Middle Woodland mound complex preserves one of the most important prehistoric mound groups in northwestern Illinois.

sites.name: Sinnissippi Park
sites.description: This park includes Hopewellian burial mounds associated with prehistoric Native American occupation in the Sterling area.

sites.name: John Deere Historic Site
sites.description: Archaeological excavations at the blacksmith shop associated with John Deere’s early career are interpreted at this historic site.

sites.name: Loveland Community House Museum
sites.description: Exhibits include prehistoric stone artifacts collected from the Dixon area within a local history museum setting.

sites.name: Northwest Territory Historic Center
sites.description: Permanent exhibit “An Unchanged Land” presents Native American history and the Black Hawk War in northwestern Illinois.

sites.name: Rock Island Arsenal Museum
sites.description: The museum’s extensive weapons exhibits include North American battlefield specimens and related military history collections.
sites.notes: Visitors use the Moline entrance to Arsenal Island.

sites.name: Colonel Davenport Home
sites.description: Artifacts found during excavations at George Davenport’s 1833 home are exhibited at this historic house site.

sites.name: Black Hawk State Historic Site Hauberg Indian Museum
sites.description: Museum exhibits include a time line with artifact displays and 18th- to 19th-century materials from Sauk and Mesquakie communities who lived nearby.

sites.name: Rock Island County Historical Society Museum
sites.description: Collections include prehistoric and historic Native American artifacts from the Quad Cities region.

sites.name: Geneseo Historical Association
sites.description: The large Italianate home, originally constructed in 1855, has displays including local American Indian artifacts.

sites.name: Bishop Hill State Historic Site
sites.description: This historic Swedish colony site includes archaeological interpretation and exhibits on nineteenth-century communal life.

sites.name: Henry County Historical Society Museum
sites.description: Museum displays include an exhibit with stone tools illustrating the prehistory of Henry County.

sites.name: Kewanee Historical Society
sites.hours: May-Oct Thu & Sat 1:30PM-4PM; Labor Day weekend 9AM-5PM
sites.description: Three floors of local history exhibits include prehistoric stone tools donated by local collectors.

sites.name: Bureau County Museum
sites.description: The museum includes Native American artifacts alongside collections on Bureau County history.
